review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the Mathlib lemmas it calls: `nonempty_sections_of_finite_cofiltered_system` and `Functor.eval_section_surjective_of_surjective` in CofilteredSystem.lean. The only repetition is in `exists_system_with` (lines 77-80) and `exists_system` (lines 92-95). Both build the same `Nonempty` and `Finite` instances for `(system p hp F hF).obj j`. That block is four lines of instance plumbing: `Sylow.nonempty`, then `finite_of_finiteIndex` on a chosen Sylow subgroup. It is not substantial repeated reasoning, so I did not report it. A local instance or a shared lemma would only slightly reduce the duplication. `exists_system` cannot be derived from `exists_system_with`, because `IsCofilteredOrEmpty J` allows an empty `J` and there is then no index `i` to start from. In the `system` definition, the `map_id` and `map_comp` proofs are routine unfolding, not repeated machinery. The ProfiniteGrp wrappers (`exists_compatibleSylowFamily_with` and `exists_compatibleSylowFamily`) are thin and similar to each other, but each only wraps one existing theorem. I found no other repeated nontrivial reasoning.
